title: surface: resolve punctuation in clicked file paths
body:
Command-click path matches can include trailing sentence punctuation or a following prose word, such as `SKILL.md again.`. The opener then receives a path that doesn't exist.

Trimming punctuation blindly isn't safe, because `.`, `;`, `?`, and `!` can all be valid filename endings on macOS. So the resolver now checks the exact accessible path first. Only after a `FileNotFound` does it try dropping a final period, followed by progressively shorter space-separated prefixes. Real filenames are preserved and sentence suffixes get dropped.

The regex span and hover highlight are unchanged, as is the existing handling of commas, trailing colons, and closers. Scheme URLs and OSC 8 links are also untouched.

Tests cover exact-path precedence, punctuation and prose-suffix fallback, home-directory caching, and OOM propagation.

The focused Zig tests and build were not run after the final changes. The available Homebrew Zig build is incompatible with this checkout, Xcode's `metal` tool is unavailable, and earlier dependency fetches failed.

Related: https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/12527

_AI disclosure: Implemented with help from Claude Code._
